name: Iriya
tagline: Tokyo in 13 minutes and Otemachi in 19 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Taito City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 19 minutes to Otemachi, 30 minutes to Shinjuku, 38 minutes to Shibuya and 27 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 2.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 7.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 2.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.6 m to 9.4 m, a difference of 7.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 7 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 5 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: ココス ナカムラ 入谷店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 12 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 台東病院, about 14 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 上宮会日暮里上宮病院, about 16 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 三ノ輪→入谷, which includes this station. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. What holds the figure down: only one line, the {line}, serving the station. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Uguisudani is ahead on rail connections and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Iriya. Uguisudani also has the JR Yamanote Line and JR Keihin-Tohoku Line, which Iriya does not. With more lines, Uguisudani is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Uguisudani is 5 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Inaricho; for lower rent, Iriya.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Iriya. Inaricho has the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, a different set from Iriya. To Shibuya, for instance, Inaricho is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Inaricho. On the number of medical facilities, Inaricho comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want another route when service is suspended
noiseSources: The 首都高速1号上野線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
昭和通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 15 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
